value.body: Digital forensics analysts collect and examine data from phones, computers and online accounts to establish what happened in fraud, data theft or criminal cases. Private forensic labs, cybersecurity firms, consulting firms and corporate investigation teams hire them. A day involves imaging devices, running analysis tools and writing reports that can stand up to scrutiny.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Forensic Science, B.Sc / B.Tech in computing, or cyber forensics courses

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Write blockers, forensic imaging and analysis suites, hash tools

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a private forensic lab or cybersecurity firm as junior analysts, often after an internship. Familiarity with operating systems, file systems and how evidence is handled is what interviewers look for.

value.title: At a glance
items: Reports may be examined in court, so documentation must be exact.
Work can involve distressing material in some cases.
Next steps: senior examiner, incident response, or cybersecurity roles.
